article.story: LOUISVILLE, Ky. -- — Imari Berry scored 18 of her 20 points in the first quarter to lead No. 3 Louisville to an 88-39 victory over Tennessee State on Tuesday night. The Cardinals (7-0), coming off a 69-51 win over No. 7 UConn, showed no hangover. Berry, who scored 21 in Sunday’s victory, had 20 points after the first 14 minutes against the Tigers (2-3) on 8-for-8 shooting, including three 3-pointers. Berry, a third-year guard who was named the Associated Press Player of the Week earlier Tuesday, played just 16 minutes and finished with four assists. Louisville led 16-5 seven minutes in and then used a 17-5 run in the final 4:01 of the first half to take a 56-26 lead at the break. The Cardinals shot 61.3% (19 for 31) in the half while holding the Tigers to 42.3% (11 for 26) and forcing 13 turnovers. Zam Jones finished with 15 points and five assists for the Cardinals. Mackenly Randolph added 12. Louisville was without Tajianna Roberts, the team’s second-leading scorer who averages 15.5 points. Coach Jeff Walz did not disclose an injury to Roberts, and said the 5-foot-10 guard is “day to day.” The Cardinals' offense slowed in the second half but their defensive intensity remained, limiting Tennessee State to 2 for 14 shooting in the fourth quarter. Grace Mbugua came off the bench and grabbed 10 rebounds for Louisville, which outrebounded Tennessee State 51-25. The Tigers committed a season-high 22 turnovers, which Louisville converted into 31 points. Somah Kamara led Tennessee State with 12 points. Up next Tennessee State: Hosts Texas-Arlington on Sunday. Louisville: Begins play in the Great Alaska Shootout on Saturday, facing host Alaska-Anchorage. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full college basketball coverage here
